lawyer:
Md Abul Hossain Azadi, Advocate------ For the Appellant. 
Md Rabiul Karim, Assistant Attorney-General------ For the State.
parties:
Tuta Pramanik (Md) ------ Accused-Appellant
vs
State ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Md Ashfaqul Islam J: This criminal appeal at the instance of the accused-appellant Md Tuta Pramanik has been preferred against the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 9-8-2004 passed by the Special Tribunal Judge No.3, Bogra in Special Tribunal Case No. 30 of 2003 convicting the appellant under section 19A and 19(f) of the Arms Act and sentencing him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period of 15 (fifteen) years and 7 years respectively and also ordered that both the sentences shall run concurrently. The Court also ordered that the total period which accused- appellant already spent in custody would be deducted from his sentence. 

 2. The prosecution case, as it appears from the deposition of the informant Md Lutfor Rahman, Officer-in-Charge of Sariakandi Police Station, Bogra, in short, is that on 27-10-2002 the informant lodged FIR with the Sariakandi Police Station alleging, inter alia, that pursuant to GD No. 319 dated 26-10-2002 on the basis of secret information he with his associate forces went to the house of the accused-appellant Tuta Pramanik and conducted search in presence of local witnesses namely, Younus Ali (PW 2), Md Rakib Uddin (PW 3), Md Bahar Ali (PW 5), Sree Arjun Roy and Robi Das Chowkider in the bedroom of a two doors tin shed house of the appellant and recovered one 9 mm pistol about 7.5" long in the body of which it is written auto pistol cal - 9 mm, 9 round, out and on the other side Automatic pistol, Made in Bulgaria. PN- 77170 with four bullets which was wrapped with polythene paper and kept inside a wooden box which was recovered as per showing and pointing out by Bulbuli, the wife of the accused appellant. The arms and ammunition were recovered by the police. Bulbuli was arrested who disclosed before the police that her husband Tuta Pramanik kept those arms and ammunition in his possession. She could not produce any valid paper in respect of said arms and ammunition. On the basis of above allegation the instant case started. 

 3. After recording of the first information report the charge of investigation was entrusted to Sub-Inspector Hasan Imam (PW 9) who on getting the responsibility visited the place of occurrence, prepared sketch map with index, examined the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and having found prima facie case submitted charge sheet against the accused appellant and his wife Bulbuli under section 19A and 19(f) of the Arms Act. The case was transmitted before the tribunal who took cognisance of the case and on the date of charge hearing on 20-5-2003 discharged accused Bulbul under section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and framed charge under section 19A and 19(f) of the Arms Act against the accused appellant Tuta Pramanik which was duly read over and explained to him to which he pleaded not guilty and demanded trial. 

 5. From the trend of cross-examination of the prosecution witnesses the defence case, as it appears, is that the accused-appellant has been falsely implicated in the instant case at the behest of his enemies which is absolutely a case of conspiracy. 

 7. Mr Md Abul Hossain Azadi, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the accused-appellant after taking us through the entire evidence on record, specially the deposition of the PWs, has submitted that in the instant case the prosecution has miserably failed to prove the allegation under section 19A and 19(f) of the Arms Act against the accused appellant beyond all reasonable doubt. He next submits that the prosecution failed to bring home the case under section 19A and 19(f) of the Arms Act in that the allegation as against the appellant that he himself kept those arms and ammunition inside the wooden box from where it was recovered could not at all be proved beyond any shadow of doubt by the prosecution and on that score, as he submits, the learned Tribunal ought to have given the appellant benefit of doubt and should have acquitted him. Elaborating his argument the learned Counsel submits that it is very unusual that though the wife of the appellant Bulbuli implicated the appellant by saying that he himself kept those arms and ammunition inside the wooden box and Bulbuli was also made an accused who was subsequently discharged by the Tribunal at the time of framing of charge but surprisingly, she was not made a witness of the case causing a serious miscarriage of justice. The learned Counsel further contends that if she would have been examined as a witness then only it could have been possible to unearth the truth of keeping the arms and ammunition in question from where it was recovered. By putting full emphasis on the above argument the learned Advocate submits that this is a fit case where the accused appellant should get benefit of doubt. 

 8. Mr Md Rabiul Karim, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the State, on the other hand, opposes the submissions of the learned Advocate for the appellant and submits that the allegation as against the appellant has been well proved by the prosecution in the instant case. All the witnesses, specially the police witnesses, have proved the prosecution case by corroborating each other to the hilt. There being no evidence to the effect that these witnesses were inimically disposed towards the accused-appellant the learned Assistant Attorney-General submits that in all fairness this appeal should be dismissed. 

 10. PW 1 Lutfor Rahman deposed the prosecution case as it has been already stated while narrating the prosecution case at the beginning. He stated that on 26-10-2002 in pursuant to GD No. 919 dated 26-10-2002 on a tip-off he raided the place of occurrence in the morning in presence of five local witnesses and recovered the alleged arms and ammunition from the house of the accused appellant as per showing and pointing out by his wife Bulbuli Begum. He also stated that the wife of the appellant Bulbuli was arrested and thereafter, seizure list was prepared in presence of witnesses. He proved seizure list Exhibit 1 and his signature therein Exhibit 1/1. He proved ejahar Exhibit 2 and his signature therein Exhibit. 2/1. He identified the alleged arms and ammunition as material Exhibits M-l, M-II, and M-III. He also proved first information report as Exhibit 3 and his signature therein Exhibit 3/1. In his cross-examination, he clearly stated that accused-appellant was not present at the time of alleged recovery. He also admitted that as per showing and pointing out of accused Bulbuli the arms and ammunition were recovered. He also admitted in cross-examination that all the seizure list witnesses are close neighbours. Besides, he denied all the suggestions put to him by the defence including the suggestion that due to bad relationship with Bulbuli he has been implicated by her falsely. 

 11. PW 2 Younus Ali is the seizure list witness who deposed that he did not see the occurrence and he put his thumb impression on the blank paper on the date of occurrence. He identified the accused-appellant on the dock. He was declared hostile by the prosecution and cross-examined, He denied the prosecution suggestion that in presence of him police recovered seized items and he witnessed the same and later on being influenced by the accused deposed falsely. In cross-examination by the defence he denied the specific suggestion of the defence that due to enmity at the behest of his enemies he has been falsely implicated in the instant case. 

 16. PW 7 Constable Abdul Mannan also deposed supporting the prosecution case like PWs 1 and 6. He was also a member of the raiding party. 

 18. PW 9 Hasan Imam is the Investigating Officer of the case who was also a member of the raiding party. He stated that at the time of recovery of arms and ammunition he was present at the place of occurrence. He further stated that being entrusted with the investigation of the case he visited the place of occurrence, prepared sketch map with index and after completing all the formalities and having found prima facie case submitted charge sheet against the appellant and his wife. He proved the sketch map as Exhibit 4 and his signature therein as Exhibit 4/1, index Exhibit 5 and signature therein Exhibit 5/1 and identified the arms and ammunition. ln his cross-examination, he categorically stated that he was present at the time of recovery. He also stated that he does not know whether the appellant was an indifferent person of escapist mentality who used to elude from practical avocations of leading normal family life. 

 20. We have gone through the entire evidence on record, specially the deposition of witnesses, FIR, charge sheet, charge, seizure list, sketch map with index and other connected papers and document thoroughly. We have also gone through memo of appeal and heard the learned Advocate for the appellant and learned Assistant Attorney-General for the State at length. As we have already discussed that the learned advocate for appellant in the instant case has mainly contended that in the instant case the prosecution has miserably failed to prove the allegation under section 19A and 19(f) of the Arms Act against the accused appellant beyond all reasonable doubt. The allegation as against the appellant that he himself kept those arms and ammunition inside the wooden box from where it was recovered could not at all be proved beyond any shadow of doubt by the prosecution and on that score as he submits, the learned tribunal ought to have given the appellant benefit of doubt and should have acquitted him. Moreover, it is also submitted that independent witnesses i.e. FIR-named three witnesses who were also cited as seizure list witnesses did not support the prosecution case and all other witnesses like PWs 1, 6, 7 and 9 are the police witnesses whose testimonies cannot be relied. 

 21. It has to be noted that from the evidence on record it is found that the appellant was not present at the time of recovery and that, as per his, wife's showing the arms and ammunition were recovered. We also find from the evidence on record that the appellant was totally ail indifferent person of escapist mentality who used to keep himself aloof from the normal avocation of family life. It is very unusual that though the wife of the appellant Bulbuli implicated the appellant by saying that he himself kept those arms and ammunition inside the wooden box and Bulbuli was also, made an accused who was subsequently discharged by the tribunal at the time of framing charge but surprisingly, she was not made a witness of the case causing serious miscarriage of justice. If she would have been examined as a witness then only it could have been possible to unearth the truth of keeping the arms and ammunition in question from where it was recovered, By putting full emphasis on the above argument the learned Advocate submits that this is a fit case where the accused appellant should get benefit of doubt. It is dangerous to sustain an allegation at section 19A and 19(f) of the Arms Act when it is not clearly proved on the facts and circumstances of a particular case that the arms and ammunition alleged to have been recovered was kept by the accused himself. The long line of decisions are available on the point. The law is very much rigid and settled on this point. Regard may be taken of the decisions reported in Bhuboni Saha vs King 2 DLR (PC) 39, Arshadullah vs State 21 DLR 694, Daud Ali Daud Hossain vs The State reported in 27 DLR 251, Abul Hasem Master vs State 44 DLR 159, 47 DLR 451, 49 DLR 167, 50 DLR 356,551 and 50 DLR 515 and so many other decisions. But from the instant case the prosecution miserably failed to unfold this vital aspect and thereby miscarriage of justice was palpably done to the accused-appellant by the Tribunal without giving benefit of doubt to the appellant on that score. 

 22. As regard submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant that in the instant case seizure list witnesses did not support the prosecution case and that PWs 1, 6, 7 and 9 all are the Police witnesses and for that reason their testimonies cannot be relied upon, we are of the view that this submission does not hold good. It is settled by the several decisions that even if independent witnesses and the seizure list witnesses- do not support the prosecution case conviction, can be given relying only upon the evidence of Police witness if it inspires confidence or worthy of credit. Mahmudul Islam alias Raton vs State 53 DLR (AD) 1, Kashem vs State 54 DLR 212, Billal Miah vs State 9 ML.R 429, Mushfiqul Islam vs State 52 DLR 593, Tariqul Islam vs State 2001 BLD 140 = 6 BLC 134, Abdur Razzaque 51 DLR 83, Kamruzzaman vs Babul Sikder 47 DLR 416, Babul vs State 5 MLR 377 and 1988 BLD 106 echoed on the same point. 

 26. The accused-appellant Md Tuta Pramanik is set at liberty forthwith, if he is not wanted in connection with any other case.
